<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, touching **10** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/stored-row-binding.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/stored-row-binding.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **16** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8afaf12d7c302072871f7e975e9dff5be5541d90` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `989b65b99fbc70ce644b6e29fc707c53e29347ac` — the merge of head `dc9f723595e4d1122bf5e907ecad039a307c2e8b` into base `8afaf12d7c302072871f7e975e9dff5be5541d90`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 989b65b99fbc70ce644b6e29fc707c53e29347ac && git checkout 989b65b99fbc70ce644b6e29fc707c53e29347ac
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8afaf12d7c302072871f7e975e9dff5be5541d90 dc9f723595e4d1122bf5e907ecad039a307c2e8b && git checkout -B drift-repro 8afaf12d7c302072871f7e975e9dff5be5541d90 && git merge --no-ff dc9f723595e4d1122bf5e907ecad039a307c2e8b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8afaf12d7c302072871f7e975e9dff5be5541d90
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8afaf12d7c302072871f7e975e9dff5be5541d90` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `dc9f723595e4d1122bf5e907ecad039a307c2e8b`
Local-runs: none

Face: declaration. The PR body and the changeset both carry `Clause-②: yes (widening: …)`. The file list has no `packages/spec/**` path and no governed path; it has 8 files, all under `.changeset/`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/` and `packages/services/service-automation/src/`. Inputs: card #28717 (body, triage, claim, os-dev-report `6562183858`), the PR body and file list, the net diff `3ee6af44fd..dc9f723595` (3 commits; `7d00bb37..dc9f7235` changes only the changeset's `Clause-②:` line), and the check-runs on this head. Code the hunks cite was read at the head with `git show`: `isServedOverrideRowOf`, `storedRowBindingOf`/`bindStoredRow`, `withRowBinding`, `packagedArtifactOwner`, SchemaRegistry `registerItem`/`getItem`/`listItems`/`unregisterItem`, and the `deleteMetaItem` → `restoreArtifactRegistryView` path.

Checks on this head: all 52 check-runs (`filter=latest`) are completed, with 37 `success`, 15 `skipped` and 0 failed, cancelled or pending. The success set includes Build Core, Test Core 1–8, Type Check (workspace, source gates, consumer gates, debt ledger), Lint (ESLint, PM dispatch-gates, the scoped and repo legs), Check Changeset, PR-body guards and the Governed Surface Queue Guard. The skips are the UI, docs, opt-in and matrix-placeholder lanes this path set does not trigger. The previous head `7d00bb37` (same code) was also all green: 35 success, 13 skipped. The dev's local runs agree, but they are the dev's evidence and are not cited as verdicts here.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Public surface: one new export, `shadowedStoredRowsOf`, from the `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` index. Right.** It is reachable from the package entry, so it widens the public surface. It is pure: it reads a non-enumerable `Symbol.for(...)` own property and returns a fresh array, `[]` for a copy, a code artifact or a body that displaced nothing. It has one consumer, the automation boot pull. `incomingTakesStoredFlowSlot` stays internal (imported by `protocol.ts` only, not re-exported). That is the right split: the slot rule has one caller, and the reader is what crosses the package boundary.
2. **Accept-set: unchanged. Right.** No write door, schema, validator or refusal is touched. What metadata authors can store is the same; the diff changes only which stored body holds the registry's bare `flow` slot, and what the boot pull lists. The `.custom` override was already admitted by #28412's accept-set. `Metadata-protocol: none` is therefore correct.
3. **Behaviour: the bare-slot rule in `hydrateOverlayIntoRegistry` (Wanted 1). Right.** `getItem(type, name)` returns the plain key first (`collection.get(name)`) and falls back to a `pkg:name` key only when the plain slot is empty. Stored rows always register bare (no `packageId`), so a loader artifact found by the fallback has no stored binding, `storedRowBindingOf` gives `undefined`, and the incoming row registers as before. The verdict reads the `package_id` column through `storedRowBindingOf` and `isServedOverrideRowOf` with the owner from `packagedArtifactOwner` (the loader's set), never a body `_packageId`. The unit test shows a package-less row that stamps `_packageId: BASE.custom` loses. `registerItem` stores the item by reference (`collection.set(storageKey, item)`), and `listItems` returns those references, so the symbol written on the held override at hydration is the one the boot pull reads. All four cases in `incomingTakesStoredFlowSlot` hold: same binding replaces itself and keeps its shadows; held override vs incoming non-override keeps the slot and records the loser; incoming override takes the slot and carries the held row; anything else is last-read-wins, as before. A name with no shipping owner, an empty slot and org-scoped rows (which return earlier) are unchanged. The early `return true` skips `registerItem` and `hydrateExpandedViewItems`. The second matters only for views, and the one caller that reads the return value checks `page` only (line ~29464). So the skip is inert for `flow`.
4. **Behaviour: the boot pull's `flatMap` over `shadowedStoredRowsOf` (Wanted 2). Right.** The carried legacy row keeps its own `null` binding, so the existing precedence ranks it `runtime`: shadowed, in the receipt, and named in the existing collision warning. No new rank, predicate, warning or error code. A runtime row can never be armed over a declared override or a package, and a carried row exists only when the name has a shipping owner, so this listing cannot arm the legacy body. The flow view (`kernel:ready`, `metadata:reloaded`, the mutation sync) does not read the carried rows.
5. **Prose-only hunks (commit `a00da81f`). Right.** The `stored-row-binding.ts` header and the `[#23233]` hydration header now match `withRowBinding` at head: the column replaces a differing body `_packageId`, or drops it for a package-less row. The `deleteMetaItem` intent comment matches `isPairRowRemoval`: `flow` only.
6. **Evidence the change discriminates. Adequate.** The dev reports red-first on main (3 of 6 red), and an ablation of the verdict call (2 of 6 red, the first pin among them) with the restore verified. The pin runs on a real kernel over a better-sqlite3 file booted twice, in both store orders, with a record change fired after the boot pull and before `kernel:ready`. Each card Wanted has a pin: Wanted 1 by the two arming cases, Wanted 2 by the two warning cases and the two controls.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/metadata-protocol: patch` and `@objectstack/service-automation: patch`. Correct under AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3: the level follows the `Metadata-protocol:` kind alone, `none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. The diff publishes one new export plus a behaviour fix in a released package, so `skip-changeset` would have been wrong and a changeset is owed. One is present.

Clause-②: yes (widening). The PR body and the changeset body both declare it, line-initial, and both carry `Metadata-protocol: none`. `(widening: …)` reads as the `widening` arm under `clause2-line.mjs`'s arm reader (the arm word followed by a non-word character). The claim had expected `no` and left the measurement to the dev; the dev measured the new export and declared `yes`, which is the right answer to 「本卡放宽接受集或扩大公开面吗」 (does this card widen the accept-set or enlarge the public surface?). It widens the public surface and leaves the accept-set as it was. Not breaking: no ADR-0087 disposition or migration is owed, and no `Skills-docs:` line is owed (kind `none`, no narrowing arm).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions`: `[]`.** Nothing to answer.
- **Out-of-scope finding (class a): the boot's `[metadata_sealed_overlay_unserved]` line counts the served `.custom` override as unserved and tells the operator to delete it.** Not this card's surface; it is a separate defect in the boot report and predates this diff. **Escalated** to the seat (`domain:server#1`) to file as its own card, as the report asks (`carrier: none`). Not a finding against this PR.
- **PR-body flag: the runtime delete of the legacy row is unmeasured.** Answered from the code at head: `deleteMetaItem` heals through `restoreArtifactRegistryView(type, name, null, …)`, which drops the plain-key slot by `(type, name)` whatever row it holds. Before this diff, the plain slot held whichever row was read last, so after a legacy-row delete it was empty in both orders. After this diff it is empty too. **Not a regression and not widened by this diff.** The automation side follows the mutation sync, which the PR body says arms from the protocol's flow view and not from the registry. This review did not trace that path further; the eviction it would answer is the same before and after this diff. Recorded, no action owed here.
- **PR-body flag: only the boot pull reads the carried rows.** Confirmed: `plugin.ts` boot pull is the one call site of `shadowedStoredRowsOf`, so the carried rows reach the boot pull and nothing else.
- **Author:** PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay write). No extra author note.
- **Wanted 2's one stated answer:** "left in place and shadowed, named in the boot warning". The PR body, the changeset and the `stored-flow-slot.ts` header all give it, and they agree.

Must-fix: none. Should-fix: none.
